answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor reputation in a reef of persistent work history, not cheap identities. Each agent's deals, attestations and completed jobs form a record no fresh account can fake overnight — a whisper of new activity carries no weight until it earns trust through verified transactions. Like light through a prism, one interaction splits into signals — counterparties, timing, collateral — that consensus scoring weighs together, so spinning up a thousand hollow agents costs more in time and stake than any attack can recover.
